title: Introduce RAG capture-and-playback proxy quickstart
author: Leah Kim
description:
Summary: Lightweight quickstart that demonstrates a local capture-and-playback proxy for RAG authoring. The proxy records tool calls, streaming deltas, and KV-cache snapshots to a compact session format and includes a replay mode with time control, latency injection, and contract validation hooks.
Motivation: authors and SREs often need a reproducible environment for debugging tool-calling behavior and streaming edge-cases (partial responses, tool fallbacks, and intermittent failures). Existing examples show isolated tool stubs or full end-to-end replays, but we lacked a small, opinionated local proxy that captures canonical traces and replays them deterministically in an authoring loop.
This quickstart targets:
- Developers authoring RAG agents who want to capture sessions from a dev/test environment and replay them locally with controlled timing
- QA engineers who need deterministic reproductions for flaky tool integrations
- Platform/solutions engineers who want to demonstrate tool contract regression tests included in CI
What this PR includes:
- quickstarts/rag-capture-proxy/README.md (tutorial + architecture diagram + CLI commands)
- quickstarts/rag-capture-proxy/proxy/ (Go micro-proxy: capture -> session format, replay -> deterministic injector)
- quickstarts/rag-capture-proxy/examples/ (sample session captures, a small sqlite-backed index for optional rerun)
- docs/snippets/rag-capture-playback.md (short docsite snippet linking to quickstart)
- CI smoke test that runs: build, run proxy in capture mode against a stubbed tool and then run replay mode asserting identical final model outputs (not token-by-token; stable result hash)
Key design choices:
- Session format is newline-delimited JSON events (timestamped, canonicalized metadata) to make it human-readable and easy to diff.
- We capture: incoming user prompt, model generation stream (deltas), tool invocation requests/responses, KV-cache checkpoints at keypoints (start/end), and proxy-level metrics (latency, status).
- Replay supports: speed factor, step-by-step interactive mode, and fault-injection rules (drop tool response, delay, or return 500).
- Contract hooks: during replay the proxy will run user-provided contract validators (simple JS/JSONPath script) to assert tool responses match schema. This enables CI to include contract checks using recorded sessions.
Checklist:
- [x] Quickstart tutorial with step-by-step commands
- [x] Micro-proxy implementation (capture + replay) with unit tests
- [x] Two sample captured sessions (happy path + tool timeout)
- [x] Docsite snippet + cross-link to existing RAG authoring docs
- [x] CI smoke test wired into existing quickstarts workflow
Local dev notes:
- Start proxy in capture mode: ./bin/proxy capture --listen :8081 --out sessions/sample-2026-02-18.ndjson
- Run a toy agent pointing tools at proxy: examples/local-agent --tool-endpoint http://localhost:8081
- Replay with latency injection: ./bin/proxy replay --session sessions/sample-2026-02-18.ndjson --speed 0.5 --inject-delay "tool:api:200ms"

Review conversation (abridged, single-threaded):
- Diego Rivera (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end. Can we make the session format backwards compatible if we later add fields? NDJSON with an envelope version should work."
- Author (Leah): "Agree, added a top-level 'schema_version' and a lightweight migration helper. See session.go lines 42-78."
- Ava Thompson (reviewer): "Contract hooks are powerful but could run arbitrary code. We need an allowlist and timeouts to keep CI safe."
- Author (Leah): "Implemented a sandboxed JS runner with 1s timeout and removed require access; documented the restriction in README."
- Samir Gupta (reviewer): "The smoke test flaked once due to port contention on CI. Suggest binding to an ephemeral port and passing it to the test harness."
- Author (Leah): "Fixed by switching to listener on :0 and exporting the assigned port to the test harness. Re-run CI."
